items.title: @scarf/scarf@1.4.0 runs code when installed (telemetry)
items.subject: @scarf/scarf@1.4.0

verified_evidence.fact: package-lock.json marks @scarf/scarf@1.4.0 with hasInstallScript: true
Used in: production
Install script published on npm: postinstall: node ./report.js
Reaches the app through juice-shop@20.4.0-SNAPSHOT → swagger-ui-express@5.0.1 → swagger-ui-dist@5.36.0 → @scarf/scarf@1.4.0

items.inference: @scarf/scarf@1.4.0 is installed in production and has an install script that runs a file called report.js. The script could be used for telemetry or, if malicious, could exfiltrate data from the host. The evidence does not prove malicious intent, but the presence of a post‑install script in a production dependency is a risk that should be examined. A reviewer should inspect the contents of report.js, verify its source and intent, and confirm that the telemetry is expected and safe.
items.remedy: Disable the telemetry (for Scarf: add "scarfSettings": {"enabled": false} to package.json, or set SCARF_ANALYTICS=false) or install with --ignore-scripts.

items.title: 10 container images are referenced by tag, not by digest
items.subject: Dockerfile, docker-compose.test.yml, infrastructure/Dockerfile, infrastructure/docker-compose.yml, test/smoke/Dockerfile

verified_evidence.fact: node:24 (tag)
gcr.io/distroless/nodejs24-debian13:latest (tag (implicit latest))

node:20.19.2-bookworm-slim (tag)
node:20.19.2-bookworm (tag)
nginx:1.28.0-alpine (tag)
juice-shop:latest (tag (latest))
redis:7.4.4-alpine (tag)
mongo:4.4.29 (tag)
alpine:latest (tag (implicit latest))

items.inference: Referencing container images by tag rather than by digest allows the image content to change without notice, which can introduce malicious code if the registry is compromised or the image is updated. The evidence lists tags such as node:24, latest, and nginx:1.28.0-alpine, all of which could point to different image layers over time. This is a risky-but-normal observation that could be exploited if an attacker pushes a malicious image under the same tag. A reviewer should first confirm the source of each image, consider pinning to a specific digest, and verify that the images come from trusted registries.
items.remedy: Pin the image by digest (image@sha256:...) so the same bytes are used every build, and update the digest deliberately.

items.inference: Out of 56 production dependencies, 36 lack npm provenance attestations, meaning their build provenance is not publicly documented. This absence could allow an attacker to supply a tampered package without detection. The evidence indicates a significant risk, though it does not confirm malicious activity. A reviewer should verify the integrity of each missing‑provenance package (e.g., via checksums or lockfile hashes), consider adding provenance where possible, and assess whether the missing attestations affect critical components.
items.remedy: Prefer versions with provenance when upgrading; for critical packages, compare the tarball with the tagged source.

items.title: 7 CI actions not SHA-pinned
items.subject: .github/workflows

verified_evidence.fact: 7 CI actions not SHA-pinned

actions/checkout@v6, calibreapp/image-actions@main, coverallsapp/github-action@v2, github/codeql-action/analyze@v3, github/codeql-action/autobuild@v3, github/codeql-action/init@v3, peter-evans/create-pull-request@v8

items.inference: Using CI actions that are not SHA-pinned means the workflow could automatically pull a newer, potentially malicious version of an action at each run. The evidence lists actions like actions/checkout@v6 and github/codeql-action/analyze@v3, which are not tied to a specific commit. This is a risky-but-normal finding because the actions could be compromised if the publisher is malicious or the action repository is hijacked. A reviewer should first check that each action comes from a reputable source, consider adding SHA pinning, and review the action code for any suspicious behavior.
items.remedy: Review the action's source, pin it to a full commit SHA, and give the workflow the minimum token permissions it needs.
